## Code, the macOS way {.light-centered .center}

A normal fenced code block renders as a traffic-light terminal window, drawn in SCSS alone.
The line-number gutter is Pandoc's, recoloured rather than reimplemented, and the copy button is Quarto's, moved into the title bar.
Line highlighting steps with `code-line-numbers`.

```python {code-line-numbers="|1-2"}
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

## Incremental reveal {.light-centered .center}

Reveal points one at a time with `{.incremental}` (use sparingly).

::: {.incremental}
- First, the claim.
- Then, the evidence.
- Last, the takeaway.
:::

## [Section]{.eyebrow}<br>Section dividers {.dark-centered .center}

Use `{.dark-centered .center}` on the header for a full-bleed navy divider.
The amber eyebrow above the title is the `.eyebrow` class.

# A title-style opener {.custom-title-slide .dark-centered .center}

[Your Name]{.quarto-title-author-name}

An `#`-level slide tagged `{.custom-title-slide}` nudges its `h1` and author name down by `5vh` and resizes them: an alternative title or section opener.
